briefFidelity: FAIL, and my own unanchored description is the evidence. The brief asks for an escapement -- a mechanism, precise and instrument-like, 'machined rather than grown', carried in fine line so it 'reads as engineering rather than as mass'. Before I had read a word of it I described these as a lace doily, a mandala, a sectioned flower head and a sea-urchin test, and I used the words wreath, petal lobes and scalloped throughout. I did not once write mechanism, instrument, machined or precise, because nothing in the sheets prompted them. The output reads grown, not machined: 1203347, 1366079, 1835793, 1991107 and 1985692 are flowers, and 1733538 reads as a spore scatter. The 'fine line' requirement is inverted -- the dominant marks are thick flat filled donuts (1243682, 1283437) and large soft-edged blurred discs, and in holdout-single-512 the blue centre is a feathered haze over a gold under-mass carrying brushed striations, which is painterly mass and the exact opposite of engineering line. Fine line does exist in the filigree cores of 1310661, 1366079, 1446330 and 1475115, but it is subordinate everywhere and is the first thing lost at 120px, so the work never reads as line-carried at the size it is browsed. What the brief DOES get: brass and slate on a dark ground is delivered exactly; the negative constraints (no teeth, hands, numerals, dial marks) are honoured; and rotational order and ring count genuinely vary, 1243682 reading roughly six-fold against 1446330's eight and 1283437's ten. Palette and prohibitions met, character missed. Only 1446330, whose discrete blue circles orbit a gold core with black between them, and 1475115's machined central scribble gesture at the commissioned object at all.
composition: There is a real and deliberate focal hierarchy, and it is the same one twelve times: fine filigree core, then a large blue or gold disc, then an outer wreath of larger rings, then in a few cases satellites. 1283437 and 1203347 are the cleanest statements of it and 1446330 the most open. It is not an even field of incident -- the centre always wins. But the frame is not used, it is merely occupied: every one of the twelve is a bounded emblem parked dead centre with equal black on all sides, so there is no compositional decision distinguishing 1366079 from 1991107. The only time the frame becomes active is by accident, when 1985692 and 1310661 outgrow their cells and get cut by the edge. One composition, repeated, plus two overflows.
collectionCoherence: The strongest axis, to the point of being the problem. All twelve are unmistakably one project: one primitive (the annulus), one centring, one two-hue palette on charcoal, one scalloped circular silhouette, one large-to-small scale progression. Even the outliers stay inside the format -- 1733538 is emptier and 1561509 and 1475115 invert the gold/blue dominance, but neither leaves the grammar. Nothing here reads as a folder of unrelated files. The coherence is bought by making the silhouette a constant, which is what starves seedVariation and thumbnailSurvival below.
palette: Chosen, restrained and on brief: ochre brass and dusty slate over charcoal, two hues and no more, with translucent stacking darkening the overlaps. The ground supports the drawing in the neutral row of 1203347, 1283437 and in 1446330, where black between the members does real structural work. Two complaints. The value range is narrow -- brass and slate sit close in luminance, so at 120px the blue centres of 1203347, 1835793 and 1991107 read as grey holes rather than as a second colour. And in the stress row the object swells until the ground is squeezed out entirely (1203347 stress, 1310661 stress), at which point the palette stops being figure-and-ground and becomes a flat two-tone field.
seedVariation: Closer to one work at twelve settings than to twelve works. The variation is real but it runs along density, overall scale and gold/blue ratio, never along shape: the silhouette is the same scalloped circle in all twelve. The genuine differences are 1733538 (nearly empty, small pale core with scattered ring-dots), 1310661 and 1985692 (large and dense enough to clip), 1475115 and 1561509 (blue-dominant, the only two that read blue at a glance), 1243682 (loose donuts drifting off the body to upper-left, lower-left and lower-right) and 1446330 (airy and open). Against those six, 1203347, 1366079, 1835793, 1991107, 1985692 and 1283437 occupy one narrow middle -- gold wreath, blue middle, filigree core -- and are separable only by fine density. The project is never at risk of stopping being one project; it is at risk of being one token.
thumbnailSurvival: Judged on holdout-seeds-120 alone: the FORMAT survives completely and the individual token mostly does not. Every cell is legibly a brass-and-slate rosette on black, and the extremes stay tellable apart -- 1733538 is instantly the empty one, 1310661 the big dense one, 1561509 and 1475115 the blue ones, 1243682 the one shedding satellites. The other seven collapse: 1203347, 1366079, 1835793, 1991107 and 1985692 reduce to the same gold scalloped disc with a blue middle. Because the silhouette is a constant, all identity is carried by internal texture, which is precisely what 120px destroys -- and the brief's fine line is the very register that dies first, so at browse size the escapement reading is not merely weak, it is unavailable. On holdout-states-120 it is worse: 1203347 stress and 1310661 stress read as flat gold squares with the scalloped outline clipped away, and 1310661 stress is undifferentiated mush.
marketResponse: Visible, but not the change that was claimed, and inverted on both halves. The brief says the mechanism should LOOSEN under volatility, members spreading apart and rings separating, then TIGHTEN as conditions settle. What the sheets show is growth and consolidation: stress makes every seed larger, paler and MORE crowded, with less ground between members, not more. 1283437 neutral has discrete gold lobes with black between them and 1283437 stress merges that wreath into a nearly solid annulus -- tightening, not separating. 1203347 stress swells until it clips all four edges and the black ground is gone. 1310661 stress fills its cell corner to corner. The settle-back also fails: recovery is not smaller or tighter than neutral in any of the four seeds, it stays at stress scale, and 1283437 recovery actually re-opens its wreath into separated lobes -- so the loosening the brief wanted under stress arrives, weakly, in the wrong state. A state transition that is legible but points the opposite way from the claim is not delivery.
tokenIdentity: Three of four hold and one breaks badly. 1283437 is the same medallion in all three states -- wreath, blue disc, gold ring-rosette -- only fuller and re-populated. 1243682 keeps its six-fold body and its drifting satellites throughout, and 1310661 stays its dense lattice while the lattice thickens. 1203347 does not survive: neutral and stress both carry a clear blue ring lattice across the centre, and in 1203347 recovery the blue has almost entirely left the work, leaving a flat gold field with three or four orphan blue crescents on it. That is a colour-identity change, not a market response -- the token has been replaced by a monochrome one, and under a brief whose recovery state is supposed to mean settling back it is the wrong transformation as well as too large a one.
artifacts: Frame clipping is the most serious and it is not rare. On holdout-seeds-256, 1985692 and 1310661 are cut at the left and right edges. On holdout-states-256 it is structural: 1203347 stress, 1203347 recovery, 1310661 stress and 1310661 recovery are all cut on all four sides, so the scalloped silhouette is squared off by the viewBox and the object reads as a crop rather than as a form. Second, medium inconsistency: in holdout-single-512 (1283437 recovery) a large soft-feathered blue disc and a gold under-mass with dark brushed striations sit beneath crisply drawn flat vector donuts, so two different media are visible in one image -- and under a brief asking for machined precision the blur reads as smudge, not atmosphere. Third, the translucent stacking produces dark blotches inside the gold mass of 1991107 and 1203347 stress that read as dirt or holes rather than as drawn shadow. Fourth, the orphan blue crescents in 1203347 recovery read as the remains of a deleted layer. 1733538 is faint enough at 120 that it borders on an empty cell.
reasoning: The gate decides this. The work is competent and genuinely coherent -- the palette is exactly the brass and slate on dark ground that was asked for, the prohibitions on teeth, hands and numerals are honoured, rotational order and ring count really do vary between 1243682, 1446330 and 1283437, and laid out together the twelve are obviously one project. But the brief commissioned an escapement: a mechanism, instrument-like, machined rather than grown, drawn in fine line so it reads as engineering rather than as mass. Having looked at all five sheets before reading a word of the brief, I independently called this a doily, a mandala, a sectioned flower head and a sea-urchin test, and described its wreaths, petal lobes and scalloped edges -- I could not have been anchored, and no mechanical word occurred to me because the pictures do not supply one. That is the mirror image of the failure the instructions name: brief says mechanism, output reads botanical. The second failure compounds it -- the brief's one dynamic claim, that the mechanism loosens under volatility and tightens as conditions settle, is contradicted on the sheet, where stress consolidates 1283437's wreath into a solid annulus and swells 1203347 and 1310661 past their frames while recovery never returns toward neutral. Fine line is the register the brief made load-bearing, and it is exactly the register that does not survive 120px, which is the size that settles this. Accomplished decorative work, but not the object commissioned.
wouldChange: Invert the mark hierarchy: make stroked line the primary register and filled mass the exception. The filigree already present in the cores of 1310661, 1366079, 1446330 and 1475115 is the right drawing -- promote it to the whole token and demote the thick filled donuts of 1243682 and 1283437 to thin concentric outlines with visible black between them. Delete the gaussian-softened discs and the brushed striations seen in holdout-single-512 entirely; a machined object has no blur. Reverse the state mapping so stress increases the gap between members and the visible ground, and recovery returns the object toward its neutral diameter, instead of the present scheme where both states simply grow. Bound the layout so nothing clips -- 1203347 stress, 1310661 stress and 1985692 must stay inside the frame, since the silhouette is the only thing that survives 120px. And since that silhouette is currently a constant circle in all twelve, let symmetry order change the OUTLINE, not just the interior, so that 1203347, 1366079, 1835793 and 1991107 stop reducing to the same thumbnail. Keep the palette and the ground unchanged; they are the one part already on brief.
